title: Dataverse: create agent users with Microsoft Entra agent identity
summary: Hold: the briefing treats a documented manual creation procedure as proof that nothing happens automatically, although Microsoft has not established that default. It also overstates what controls availability and infers a manual migration mechanism that Microsoft has not documented.

claims.quote: an Entra agent user must be created and associated with the agent identity so that appropriate security roles can be assigned to enable access to Dataverse APIs and data within the environment.

claims.claim: The feature is admin-opt-in and nothing happens until an administrator adds an agent user.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: Migration from existing Dataverse application users to Dataverse agent users is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse agent user migration application users; Dataverse agent users enable migration. Read admin/agent-users and create-users. Copilot Studio app-registration identity migration is documented, but no Dataverse application-user-to-agent-user migration procedure was found.

claims.claim: Any move from existing application users to agent users is a manual piece of work.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse agent user migration application users. Read admin/agent-users and create-users. Neither gives a migration mechanism; absence of a documented migration does not establish that it is manual.
claims.fix: Remove 'so any move is a manual piece of work to plan'. Keep only 'Microsoft has not documented migration from existing application users to agent users at the time of writing (November 2026)'.

claims.claim: An API or script specifically documented for provisioning a Dataverse agent user and assigning its role has not been published.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse agent user API; Dataverse agent users PowerShell pac; Dataverse agent user provisioning Power Platform API systemuser agenttype Add-AdminPowerAppsSyncUser. Read feature pages and PAC/PowerShell excerpts; generic user APIs do not explicitly confirm agent provisioning.

claims.claim: The create-an-agent-user section does not name a required administrator role.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse agent user required role. Read create-users#create-an-agent-user-preview in full: the ten steps name no required role. This confirms only the section's omission, not the absence of platform role requirements.

claims.claim: No dedicated tenant-wide Dataverse agent-users enable/disable switch is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse agent users tenant switch; Dataverse agent users enable migration. Read admin/agent-users, create-users and disable-agent-identities. Found general Entra blocking and creation restrictions, not a dedicated Dataverse agent-users availability switch.

claims.claim: Dataverse agent-user availability is controlled by who can reach environment settings and by Entra's ability to create identities.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse agent user required role; Dataverse agent users tenant switch. Read feature creation pages and Entra creation/disable guidance. No source defines reaching environment settings as the access control or establishes this complete availability mechanism.
claims.fix: Remove the clause 'availability is controlled by who can reach the environment settings and by Entra's ability to create agent identities'. The separate finding about the missing tenant-switch row calls for removing the rest of that sentence too.

claims.claim: Environment auditing must be enabled before enabling table and column auditing for data changes.

claims.quote: Dataverse stores audit logs and they consume log storage capacity.

claims.quote: We recommend applying these policies in report-only mode first to understand their impact before enforcing them.
